result.topic_en: Euler continues a computation making $3a+y$ a square via a quadratic root ansatz, then gives an annotation showing that if $mx^3+kk$ is a square at $x=a$, two further cases $x=-2ak/(b+k)$ and $x=2ak/(b-k)$ follow, with the example $90x^3+1$.
result.transcription:
cujus radix ponatur $b+\frac{3maa}{2b}y$; hujus quadratum
$bb+3maay+\frac{9mma^4}{4bb}yy$ praebet
$3a+y=\frac{9ma^4}{4bb}=\frac{9a(bb-n)}{4bb}$
unde $y=-\frac{3a}{4}-\frac{9an}{4bb}$, ergo $x=\frac{a}{4}-\frac{9an}{4bb}$. Sin autem radix ponatur $b+\frac{3maa}{2b}y+pyy$, erit
$3mayy+my^3=2bpyy+\frac{9mma^4}{4bb}yy+\frac{3mpaay^3}{b}+ppy^4$.
Jam fiat $3ma=2bp+\frac{9mma^4}{4bb}=2bp+\frac{9am(bb-n)}{4bb}$, ergo
$2bp=3ma-\frac{9am(bb-n)}{4bb}=\frac{3ma}{4}+\frac{9amn}{4bb}$, ergo
$p=\frac{3ma}{8b}+\frac{9amn}{8b^3}=\frac{3ma}{8b}\left(1+\frac{3n}{bb}\right)$.
Superest haec aequatio $1=\frac{3paa}{b}+\frac{ppy}{m}$, ergo
$\frac{ppy}{m}=1-\frac{3paa}{b}=1-\frac{9ma^3}{8bb}-\frac{27a^3mn}{8b^4}=-\frac{1}{8}+\frac{9n}{8bb}-\frac{27n}{8bb}+\frac{27nn}{8b^4}$
$=-\frac{1}{8}-\frac{9n}{4bb}+\frac{27nn}{8b^4}$, ergo $y=\frac{m}{8pp}\left(-1-\frac{18n}{bb}+\frac{27nn}{b^4}\right)$.
(Lexell.)
Annotatio ad superiorem formulam $mx^3+n=\Box$, ubi ex dato casu $ma^3+n=bb$ ope transformationis elicuimus novum casum.
Omni attentione dignum videtur, quod si $n$ fuerit numerus quadratus $=kk$, ex casu cognito $ma^3+kk=bb$ immediate duo alii elici queant hoc modo: Ponatur $x=az$, ut habeatur $ma^3z^3+kk=\Box$, hoc est
$(bb-kk)z^3+kk=\Box=yy$, ita ut sit $(bb-kk)z^3=yy-kk=(y+k)(y-k)$.
Resolvetur ergo formula $(bb-kk)z^3$ etiam in duos factores, quod duplici modo fieri potest:
I. Sit unus factor $(b+k)zz=y+k$, eritque alter $(b-k)z=y-k$, haec aequatio ab illa subtracta relinquit $(b+k)zz-(b-k)z=2k$, cujus una radix manifesto est $z=1$, unde pro altera fit
$z=\frac{-2k}{b+k}$, ergo $x=\frac{-2ak}{b+k}$.
II. Sit jam prior factor $(b-k)zz=y-k$, et alter dabit $(b+k)z=y+k$, unde fit differentia
$(b-k)zz-(b+k)z=-2k$,
cujus una radix est $z=1$, et altera $z=\frac{2k}{b-k}$ et $x=\frac{2ak}{b-k}$.
Unde conficimus istud egregium THEOREMA:
Si formula $mx^3+kk$ fuerit quadratum casu $x=a$, ita ut sit $ma^3+kk=bb$, tum etiam quadratum erit his duobus casibus:
primo: $x=\frac{-2ak}{b+k}$, et altero: $x=\frac{+2ak}{b-k}$.
Exempli gratia, cum formula $90x^3+1$ fiat quadratum casu $x=\frac{1}{2}$; fiet enim $90\cdot\frac{1}{8}+1=\frac{49}{4}$, ubi est $a=\frac{1}{2}$, $k=1$ et $b=\frac{7}{2}$, bini casus derivati erunt $x=-\frac{2}{9}$ et $x=+\frac{2}{5}$; ex priore enim fit $\frac{-10.8}{81}+1=\frac{1}{81}$,
et ex posteriore $\frac{90.8}{5^3}+1=\frac{18.8}{25}+1=\frac{169}{25}$.
A. m. T. I. p. 120. 121.

methods.what: Finding a new rational point by setting the square root equal to a linear ansatz in y
Quadratic root ansatz with parameter p chosen to cancel the yy terms, giving another solution
Factorization $(bb-kk)z^3=(y+k)(y-k)$ split into two factors to derive new solutions

methods.what: Theorem: from one solution of $mx^3+k^2=\square$ two others follow
methods.quote:

primo: $x=\frac{-2ak}{b+k}$, et altero: $x=\frac{+2ak}{b-k}$.

items.quote:
Si formula $mx^3+kk$ fuerit quadratum casu $x=a$, ita ut sit $ma^3+kk=bb$, tum etiam quadratum erit his duobus casibus:
primo: $x=\frac{-2ak}{b+k}$, et altero: $x=\frac{+2ak}{b-k}$.
items.english: If the formula $mx^3+kk$ is a square for $x=a$, so that $ma^3+kk=bb$, then it will also be a square in these two cases: first $x=-2ak/(b+k)$, and second $x=+2ak/(b-k)$.
